rationale: The v2.6.0 deprecation entry that shipped in a release is deleted from asset.dto.ts's history rather than superseded, while search.dto.ts still carries both the v2.6.0 and 'v3: -1 no longer valid' entries, so the two published histories now contradict each other. Real but small; the substantive half (search still rejecting -1) is g14.

A considered-and-cleared note: the 'Using 0 as a rating is no longer valid' entry is accurate (0 was previously coerced to null by a transform, now rejected by the refine); the residual point that the history does not mention -1 being re-allowed is a wording preference already covered by g01.

Zod 4's util.extend keeps the object's checks (it only throws when the new shape overwrites an existing key), and the refine/extend pattern is untouched by the diff and exercised by the existing lat/long tests; a 'worth confirming' note with no defect.
Considered-and-cleared: `Rating: tags.rating === null ? 0 : tags.rating` passes -1 through; asserts no defect.
Explains a diff-rendering artifact for generated files; no defect asserted.

The merge loop takes the max rating starting from 0 and only writes it when > 0, so a -1 duplicate merged into an unrated keeper leaves the keeper unrated; correct trace of pre-existing behavior that -1 makes reachable again, but whether a rejection should propagate to the keeper is debatable, so it is small.

-1 is truthy so it is passed as Rating and StarRating fills no stars ((-1||0) >= value is false), so a rejected asset looks unrated apart from the 'clear' button; a real, pre-existing web gap the server-only PR re-exposes, but out of the PR's scope and longstanding.
Considered-and-cleared: the generated Dart model does no range enforcement; asserts no defect.

At the diff's base commit rating 0 was already rejected by .min(1) (introduced by #27896, marked refactor!), so this PR does not introduce the 0->400 change; and the diff itself documents it via the new 'v3: Using 0 as a rating is no longer valid' history entry. Only the 'no test pins 0' kernel is true, and it is minor.

Mostly a cleared suspicion: 3.5 yields only the int error (invalid_type is aborting, continue:false), and an unsafe integer like 1e21 yields a non-aborting too_big plus the refine message; two error strings on a nonsense input is cosmetic and not worth reviewer attention.
Commit-message typos on a PR that will be squash-merged; not a code concern.
Stylistic preference about the refine error string; the message is accurate and unambiguous. Not the same substance as thread 2, which is about the .describe() text.

True that main-branch databases which ran the migration in the ~3-day window (v3.0.0 unreleased; last tag v2.7.5) had -1 set to NULL irreversibly, but no remediation is possible and the affected population is pre-release; the actionable part of the migration-deletion concern is g22.

BaseSearchSchema.rating still has .min(1).max(5) and the 'v3: Using -1 as a rating is no longer valid' history entry, so all derived search DTOs return 400 for rating -1 after this PR makes -1 settable, and the search and asset histories now contradict each other. Incomplete revert of #27896, not raised by any thread.

options[0] is the 'null' entry and options[1..5] are ratings 1..5, so options[rating] is not off by one; Number.parseInt('null') is NaN but serializes to JSON null, which is what the search API expects for unrated. Also pre-existing and unrelated to the diff by its own admission.

Moving the bounds into .refine() leaves z.int()'s safe-integer bag min/max as the only emitted bounds, so the spec and generated clients publish minimum -9007199254740991 / maximum 9007199254740991 for the rating field; this is exactly thread 1's 'wrong/misleading' comment on that spec line.

The as-is loop still tests only ratings 1 and 5, and the negative-rating e2e and metadata.service.spec cases removed by #27896 are not restored, so nothing in CI asserts -1 is accepted; correct and actionable, small to fix.
Both boundary cases now assert the same refine message, an inherent consequence of a single refine; the test still fails on a wrong status or message, so this is a preference, not a defect.

The three rating field descriptions now disagree ('-1 (rejected)' vs '[1-5], or null' vs 'Rating') and the rejected semantics are documented nowhere; true and actionable but small, and the search half largely follows from g14.
Considered-and-cleared note that other rating consumers are unaffected; asserts no defect.

metadata extraction still uses validateRange(exifTags.Rating, 1, 5), which returns null for -1, while handleSidecarWrite writes Rating -1 to the sidecar and then unlocks the property; so a -1 set via the API (or authored externally as XMP rejected) is silently dropped to NULL on the next extraction. #27896 changed this from (-1, 5) and this PR does not revert it.

runMigrations uses Kysely's Migrator with a FileMigrationProvider and rethrows any error; Kysely's migrator throws 'corrupted migrations: previously executed migration ... is missing' unconditionally when a recorded migration is absent from the folder, so any database that ran the now-deleted file (main/RC builds in the window since #27896) fails at startup. Confidence tempered because the population is pre-release only.

ExifResponseSchema.rating is still z.int().min(1).max(5) (added by #27896) so the published response contract says 1..5 while the server can now return -1; no runtime failure because no controller uses ZodSerializerDto, but the spec is wrong for consumers.
Considered-and-cleared: .nullable() then .refine() accepting null then .optional() behaves the same as .nullish() for omitted/null values; asserts no defect.
True that -1 is truthy and counts toward the EXIF tie-break, but a rejected asset does carry rating information, and this only nudges a size tie-break; pre-existing and not worth reviewer attention.

Considered-and-cleared: widening request-property bounds is not a breaking change for oasdiff's fail-on ERR gate; asserts no defect.
